summary.text: Nate Marsh is the Republican candidate for Colorado House of Representatives District 43 in the November 3, 2026 general election, having advanced from the Republican primary on June 30, 2026.

A senior deputy district attorney who has served in the Douglas County District Attorney's Family Violence Unit since 2021, he said in a Ballotpedia survey that he is running to bring prosecutorial experience to the legislature and to restore affordability.

paragraphs.text: In a Ballotpedia survey, Nate Marsh said he was born in Montana and raised in Highlands Ranch.
He earned a political science degree from Texas Christian University and a law degree from the University of Maryland.

During law school he worked at the Baltimore City State's Attorney's Office, and after returning to Colorado he joined the District Attorney's Office in El Paso County, where he handled cases ranging from DUIs to first-degree murder and later prosecuted sexual offenses against children.

Since 2021 he has served in the Family Violence Unit in Douglas County, and he said he received the Colorado District Attorney Council Faculty Member of the Year recognition for his training and advocacy.
Marsh said his key campaign messages include restoring affordability by protecting TABOR, cutting unnecessary regulations and refocusing state spending.
He also said Colorado needs a justice system that puts victims first.
